analysis: All three changed files are test-only, so no production behavior changes in this batch. (1) FlintContextAdmissionTests.swift:179 changes the test slot's kvBackendConfig from "contiguous" to "paged". This matches the new paged-only Flint contract; the test still replaces the engine with a sentinel and sets PrefixCachePolicy.environmentFlag to "0", so the SSD prefix cache (T-041) is not exercised. (2) FlintPagedOnlyBackendTests.swift (new) asserts that auto and paged resolve to paged, that the crash-loop guard does not downgrade Flint to contiguous, and that explicit contiguous and the paged kill switch throw EngineV2ProductionError. It uses a temp-file guard path under the test's own directory and /dev/null elsewhere, with cleanup via defer. These tests add regression coverage for fail-closed backend selection and add no new attack surface. (3) FlintPolicyTests.swift:131-143 asserts that the provider-wide global quantization default never blocks Flint, while per-model and environment overrides to a non-native value still throw flintRequiresNative. This is test coverage for a policy change implemented elsewhere. The production sources (EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend, EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve, the KVBackendGuard logic) were not supplied. So I could not verify that the production behavior matches these tests, in particular that the global-default relaxation cannot let a non-native KV quantization reach Flint through some other path, or that the contiguous refusal is enforced. No threat-model assertion is weakened by the tests themselves. Integration should confirm the corresponding production diff (backend refusal and global-default handling) against TB-007, T-041 and T-028, since this batch contains no production code.
